```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>"
)

has_runtime_pkgs <-
    requireNamespace("targets", quietly = TRUE) &&
        requireNamespace("codetools", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_runtime_pkgs)
```

`execute_pipeline()` recomputes every series on every run. For pipelines that
run regularly, or that contain slow steps, [targets](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/)
can keep results between runs and recompute only what changed. This vignette
shows three ways of combining the two:

- caching `execute_pipeline()` results with a single option,
- a full `targets` project built with `tar_tsflow()`, including tracked data
  files and missing inputs,
- lineage documentation that `targets` keeps up to date.

The patterns follow the [targets manual](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/):
its walkthrough (tracked data files), literate programming (documents as
targets) and distributed computing chapters.

## Example: Monthly Retail Sales

The example turns monthly nominal retail sales and a consumer price index into
real, seasonally adjusted sales, a year-on-year growth rate and a trend.

```{r}
library(tsflow)

set.seed(42)
months <- 120
price_index <- ts(
    100 * cumprod(1 + rnorm(months, 0.002, 0.002)),
    start = c(2015, 1),
    frequency = 12
)
seasonal_pattern <- rep(c(-8, -10, -2, 0, 1, 2, 0, -1, 1, 3, 8, 16), months / 12)
real_sales <- 200 + 0.5 * seq_len(months) + seasonal_pattern + rnorm(months, 0, 2)
sales_nominal <- ts(real_sales * price_index / 100, start = c(2015, 1), frequency = 12)

inputs <- list(sales.nominal = sales_nominal, cpi = price_index)
```

The pipeline, with two shared parameters:

```{r}
pipeline_lines <- c(
    "vars:",
    "  base_year: 2020",
    "  trend_window: 12",
    "series:",
    "  - name: sales.nominal",
    "    source: {type: injected}",
    "  - name: cpi",
    "    source: {type: injected}",
    "  - name: sales.nominal.sa",
    "    expr: \"seasonal_adjust(sales.nominal)\"",
    "  - name: sales.real",
    "    expr: \"deflate(sales.nominal, cpi, base_year = @base_year)\"",
    "  - name: sales.real.sa",
    "    expr: \"seasonal_adjust(sales.real)\"",
    "  - name: sales.growth",
    "    expr: \"base::round(growth_rate(sales.real.sa, lag = 12), digits = 1)\"",
    "  - name: sales.trend",
    "    expr: \"moving_average(sales.real.sa, n = @trend_window)\""
)
pipeline_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "retail.yml")
writeLines(pipeline_lines, pipeline_path)
cat(pipeline_lines, sep = "\n")
```

And its transforms, plain R functions:

```{r}
# Real values in prices of `base_year`.
deflate <- function(nominal, prices, base_year) {
    base_level <- mean(window(prices, start = c(base_year, 1), end = c(base_year, 12)))
    nominal / (prices / base_level)
}

# Remove a fixed seasonal pattern.
seasonal_adjust <- function(x) {
    fit <- stats::stl(x, s.window = "periodic")
    x - fit$time.series[, "seasonal"]
}

# Growth in percent over `lag` periods (12 = year on year).
growth_rate <- function(x, lag = 12) {
    100 * (x / stats::lag(x, -lag) - 1)
}

# Trailing moving average over `n` periods.
moving_average <- function(x, n = 12) {
    stats::filter(x, rep(1 / n, n), sides = 1)
}

transforms <- list(
    deflate = deflate,
    seasonal_adjust = seasonal_adjust,
    growth_rate = growth_rate,
    moving_average = moving_average
)
```

## Cache Results With One Option

Setting `tsflow.store` makes `execute_pipeline()` run through `targets` behind
the scenes and keep its results in that directory. No `_targets.R` is needed.
`result$rebuilt` lists the series recomputed in a run.

```{r}
options(tsflow.store = file.path(tempdir(), "tsflow-cache"))

first <- execute_pipeline(pipeline_path, inputs = inputs, transforms = transforms)
first$rebuilt
```

Running again with nothing changed recomputes nothing:

```{r}
second <- execute_pipeline(pipeline_path, inputs = inputs, transforms = transforms)
second$rebuilt
```

Changing a transform recomputes only the series that use it. Here the growth
rate switches from year-on-year to month-on-month by changing the default:

```{r}
year_on_year_growth_rate <- growth_rate
growth_rate <- function(x, lag = 1) {
    100 * (x / stats::lag(x, -lag) - 1)
}
transforms$growth_rate <- growth_rate

third <- execute_pipeline(pipeline_path, inputs = inputs, transforms = transforms)
third$rebuilt
```

Only `sales.growth` was recomputed, even though the pipeline still passes
`lag = 12`: `targets` compares the function's code, not its result. Changes to
helper functions that a transform calls are detected the same way.

`store = NULL` in a call, or unsetting the option, goes back to in-memory
execution. The rest of the vignette uses the year-on-year growth rate again:

```{r}
options(tsflow.store = NULL)
growth_rate <- year_on_year_growth_rate
transforms$growth_rate <- growth_rate
```

## A targets Project

For larger pipelines, or to combine tsflow series with other work such as
models and reports, use `tar_tsflow()` in a regular `targets` project. It turns
the pipeline into targets: by default one per step, with the last step of each
series named after the series.

The project below lives in a temporary directory. The raw data is a file that
`targets` tracks (`format = "file"`), and the transforms live in a script that
`_targets.R` sources, as is usual in `targets` projects.

```{r}
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "retail-targets")
dir.create(project, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(pipeline_lines, file.path(project, "retail.yml"))
dump(c("deflate", "seasonal_adjust", "growth_rate", "moving_average"), file.path(project, "transforms.R"))
saveRDS(inputs, file.path(project, "inputs.rds"))

targets_script <- c(
    "library(targets)",
    "source(\"transforms.R\")",
    "",
    "list(",
    "  tar_target(inputs_file, \"inputs.rds\", format = \"file\"),",
    "  tar_target(tsflow_inputs, readRDS(inputs_file)),",
    "  tsflow::tar_tsflow(",
    "    \"retail.yml\",",
    "    transforms = list(",
    "      deflate = deflate,",
    "      seasonal_adjust = seasonal_adjust,",
    "      growth_rate = growth_rate,",
    "      moving_average = moving_average",
    "    )",
    "  )",
    ")"
)
writeLines(targets_script, file.path(project, "_targets.R"))
cat(targets_script, sep = "\n")
```

You would normally run `targets` functions from the project directory. In this
vignette, two small helpers do that. `make()` returns the derived series and
steps that were built; the raw series and the data file targets are left out,
since they are reloaded whenever the data file changes:

```{r}
in_project <- function(code) {
    old <- setwd(project)
    on.exit(setwd(old))
    code
}

make <- function() {
    in_project(targets::tar_make(reporter = "silent", callr_function = NULL))
    progress <- in_project(targets::tar_progress())
    built <- progress$name[progress$progress == "completed"]
    setdiff(built, c("inputs_file", "tsflow_inputs", "sales.nominal", "cpi"))
}
```

`tar_manifest()` lists the targets `tar_tsflow()` created. `sales.growth` has
two steps, so its first step is a target of its own, `sales.growth..step1`:

```{r}
in_project(targets::tar_manifest(fields = "name", callr_function = NULL))
```

The first run builds everything, and `tar_read()` returns any series:

```{r}
make()
window(in_project(targets::tar_read(sales.growth)), start = c(2024, 1))
```

A second run builds nothing:

```{r}
make()
```

### Changing a Parameter

Changing a shared parameter reruns only the steps that use it. A shorter trend
window affects only the trend:

```{r}
pipeline_file <- file.path(project, "retail.yml")
writeLines(sub("trend_window: 12", "trend_window: 6", readLines(pipeline_file)), pipeline_file)

make()
```

Moving the base year changes the real series, and with it everything computed
from real sales, but not `sales.nominal.sa`:

```{r}
writeLines(sub("base_year: 2020", "base_year: 2018", readLines(pipeline_file)), pipeline_file)

make()
```

### Changing the Data

Editing the tracked data file reloads the raw series, but steps only rerun
when their inputs actually changed: revising the CPI reruns everything
computed from real sales, while `sales.nominal.sa` is left alone because
`sales.nominal` itself did not change.

```{r}
revised <- inputs
revised$cpi <- revised$cpi * 1.01
saveRDS(revised, file.path(project, "inputs.rds"))

make()
```

### Missing Inputs

If a raw series is not available, it and everything that depends on it hold a
placeholder instead of a value, and the rest of the pipeline still builds:

```{r}
saveRDS(list(sales.nominal = sales_nominal), file.path(project, "inputs.rds"))

make()
in_project(targets::tar_read(sales.real))
window(in_project(targets::tar_read(sales.nominal.sa)), start = c(2024, 7))
```

Raw series can also come from loaders for their `source` type instead of an
inputs list; see `?tar_tsflow` and the README section "Loading Raw Data".
Loader targets rerun on every `tar_make()`, because `targets` cannot see
whether external data changed, but downstream steps only rerun when the loaded
values differ.

## Documentation as a Target

`document_pipeline()` writes lineage pages for every series. As a target that
depends on the pipeline file, the pages are regenerated whenever the
definition changes, and are otherwise left alone:

```{r}
saveRDS(inputs, file.path(project, "inputs.rds"))

docs_script <- c(
    targets_script[-length(targets_script)],
    "  ,",
    "  tar_target(pipeline_file, \"retail.yml\", format = \"file\"),",
    "  tar_target(",
    "    lineage_docs,",
    "    tsflow::document_pipeline(",
    "      tsflow::plan_pipeline(",
    "        pipeline_file,",
    "        transforms = list(deflate = deflate, seasonal_adjust = seasonal_adjust,",
    "                          growth_rate = growth_rate, moving_average = moving_average)",
    "      ),",
    "      \"lineage\"",
    "    ),",
    "    format = \"file\"",
    "  )",
    ")"
)
writeLines(docs_script, file.path(project, "_targets.R"))

invisible(make())
basename(in_project(targets::tar_read(lineage_docs)))
```

## Parallel Workers

`targets` can run independent steps in parallel through
[crew](https://wlandau.github.io/crew/). This pays off when steps are slow, for
example seasonal adjustment of hundreds of series. Add a controller to
`_targets.R`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(targets)
tar_option_set(controller = crew::crew_controller_local(workers = 4))
```

`tar_make()` then sends ready steps to the workers. `tar_visnetwork()` shows the
graph of step targets with their status, and `tar_meta()` holds timings and any
errors per step.

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(project, recursive = TRUE)
```
